newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany expects to meet EMU criteria in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Germany expects to meet EMU criteria in 1997.

text.p: The German government still expects to be able to meet the strict fiscal targets this year to qualify for Europe's single currency in 1999, the finance ministry said on Friday.

"Germany will be below the deficit criteria ," a ministry spokeswoman told reporters, adding that the deficit targets could be met even if tax revenues end up weaker than forecast as was the case in 1996.
The spokeswoman, responding to questions after a newspaper report, said the government had not yet decided whether to impose a spending freeze in order to rein in widening budget deficits.

The economic daily Handelsblatt, citing unnamed government sources, said on Friday that Bonn was increasingly concerned it will not be able to restrict the budget deficit this year to under three percent, as required to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The paper said Finance Minister Theo Waigel would impose a public spending freeze this month.
